cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Not the Real Fear
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on practical details so no one reaches the fear underneath them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll have tea, then open my scholarship letter. Find two clean teaspoons.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made your tea. Open it; I want to know if you're leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put sugar in mine. I'll wash the cups if you make it again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take mine. Are you frightened of going, or staying here with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mine can be yours, then. Find a pen; I'll label them before we drink.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sets the tea-before-letter agenda; A3 offers washing to get B to remake tea; A5 accepts B swap while assigning labeling to keep the talk practical.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 made tea, A3 sugar and B4 alternative cup are consistent; A5 labels are excessive avoidance rather than a factually required solution.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the consequential letter opened and B4 both solves the drink problem and asks the emotional question.

heightening.evidence: B4 cup swap removes A3 obstacle; A5 turns the solution into another task instead of answering the fear question.

specificity.evidence: A1 scholarship letter and B2 possible departure make the stakes legible; the exact feared outcome can remain uncertain.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 acceptance, pen request and A own labeling task negotiate work rather than summarize avoidance.
